newsitem.title: UK: London gold firmer, eyeing the upside.
newsitem.headline: London gold firmer, eyeing the upside.

text.p: Gold prices were firmer on Tuesday morning, and dealers said the market could be due for an upside push following weeks of rapid losses.
Bullion fixed at $346.30 an ounce, up $2.00 from the previous fixing on Monday afternoon but little changed from firmer London closing levels.

"There was a bit of down and up after prices came down overnight, but it's been fairly steady this morning," a bullion dealer said. "The question is, can we break through $346.50, which has stopped gold for the past two days. If we can, it could get the funds involved and trigger some stop loss buying."
The bullion market was oversold and a foray towards the psychological $350 an ounce level was anticipated, technical analysts said.
But gold's steep downtrend was most likely still in effect and gains would be shortlived, analysts said.

Prices, already at 3-1/4 year lows, had briefly pushed just below an important 12-year support line last week. That left gold vulnerable to more losses. "I suspect we'll see the market try to regain $350, fail miserably and come lower," said analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
Recent lows around $343.50 would cushion a decline, but $340 was the critical support level.
The market was expecting little direction from the U.S. Federal Reserve's two day meeting, which starts on Tuesday. Analysts expected the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged amid tame inflation.
"The feeling is there won't be any surprises. They're not likely to change interest rates which means little effect on the market," a dealer said.
The other metals were also little changed from Monday's London close.
Silver was steady at $4.90/$4.92 an ounce, and expected to consolidate in a tight range for the time being, while platinum at $351.25/$352.25, was barely lower.
Palladium, last quoted at $125.50/$126.50, was also stable but dealers said it had the potential to extend it recent gains. Prices have climbed some $12 since last December.
Dealers have attributed its rise to delays in the 1997 export contract talks between Japan and Russia for platinum group metals.
